text:
ada: heads-up, noticed ~20% p95 regression on CPU workers after the batching heuristic change in PR#3121 — mainly CPU-side. Repro on staging with load test.
ada: ran perf sampling on the worker; top symbols are in tokenization and scheduler wake paths. pasted a minimal excerpt below.
ada: ```
Samples: 500K of event 'cycles'
  12.4%  redwood_worker  [.] token::tokenize_batch
  9.1%   redwood_worker  [.] scheduler::schedule_next_batch
  7.8%   python3.10      [.] PyObject_Call
  6.2%   libc-2.31.so    [.] __memcpy_sse2_unaligned
```
kevin: can you also paste the perf script stacks (folded) or flame SVG? want to see callchains.
ada: attaching condensed folded output inline (filtered to python + runtime):
ada: ```
redwood_worker token::tokenize_batch;python_tokenize;PyUnicode_Decode;_PyUnicode_Ready 120
redwood_worker scheduler::schedule_next_batch;batch::prepare;PyObject_Call 90
redwood_worker kvcache::lookup;memcpy 40
```
lucy: 2 quick thoughts: (1) did we change sync points in batching that force tokenizers to run on main thread? (2) GIL churn looks plausible from the PyObject_Call samples.
srinivas: agree. The scheduler->batch prepare path does an allocator hop then calls into Python callback on the worker thread; if batching triggers more frequent small batches we'll see more GIL grabs.
kevin: @ada can you run `perf record -F 199 -g -- ./redwood_worker --config staging` and then `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded`? also try `perf sched` to see wakeup hotspots.
ada: did both. `perf sched` shows a lot of `sched_wake_up` and `futex_wake` around the batching window. snippet:```
prio 0: wake_up: task redwood_worker/12 -> runnable (latency 120us)
futex_waiters: futex(0x7f...) -> 3 waiters, wakeups 420
```
lucy: futex chatter + short latencies = high syscalls overhead. tokenization is also mem-bound; memcpy shows up. could be smaller batch sizes increasing memcpy frequency.
srinivas: let's try a targeted experiment: roll back the batching tweak on staging (use old batch window of 32 tokens) and re-run perf. if p95 goes back -> batching is root cause.
ada: rolled back to old heuristic on a staging cluster and re-ran the same load. p95 improved ~18%, perf samples now:```
  6.1%  redwood_worker [.] token::tokenize_batch
  4.0%  redwood_worker [.] scheduler::schedule_next_batch
  3.9%  python3.10   [.] PyObject_Call
```
kevin: nice. that points to change in batching causing more frequent tokenization on main threads. can we instead coalesce tokenization work onto a pool thread so GIL grabs are amortized?
lucy: we have a small tokenization threadpool in the runtime but it was bypassed for short batches to avoid latency. maybe need a threshold bump.
srinivas: also consider sampling the batch size distribution to pick heuristic — maybe we biased towards small batches too aggressively.
ada: opened a tiny revert PR with a perf/latency test in CI + perfjob link: https://perf.internal/runs/3121-rollback-try.
perf-bot: CI perf test detected p95 delta: -17% (regression reverted). Report: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/3121/perf-summary
kevin: for long-term: add `perf record` CI hook for CPU-hotpath changes + a small script that auto-runs perf against microbench tokenization/scheduler and stores folded stacks. then we can diff folded stacks across commits.
lucy: also add ops metric: futex wakeups/sec and GIL hold time (using pyinstrument/py-spy) to the per-route dashboards. makes regressions easier to pinpoint.
srinivas: one more: run `perf record -e cycles:u -c 50 -g --` at higher sampling to get deeper stacks for memcpy/KV cache interactions. Ada, can you schedule that next?
ads: will run tomorrow morning on staging with a dedicated perf node (low noise).
ada: thanks all, saved the folded stacks in the perf job; will follow up with flame SVG and a short writeup on root cause and concrete fix (bump tokenization threadpool threshold + tweak heuristic). :thumbsup:
